observations: Photo 0 shows a large flat-screen LG TV on a wall with a soundbar/box on the stand; the screen is on and displays the webOS home interface.
Photo 0 shows a visible LG logo on the bottom bezel area.
Photo 1 shows the TV screen playing a beach/sea scene; no obvious screen lines are visible in the photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows an LG logo on the TV bezel.
No measurement, model label, or scale reference that confirms 86-inch size in photo 0 or photo 1.
The model number is not readable on the TV in photo 0 or photo 1.
The photos show the TV is on, but do not show a resolution/specs screen or a readable model/spec label.
webOS is visible (photo 0), but the specific 'AI' features and 'advanced' claims are not verifiable from the photos.

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen, remote included.
claims.evidence: Photo 1 does not show obvious lines/dead pixels, but there is no full-screen test pattern and the remote is not shown.
No service/repair history documentation is shown; photos cannot confirm repair status.

risks.risk: Exact model/size may differ (price depends heavily on 86-inch and the specific LG series).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the TV's rear label/model sticker (including model number) and/or the TV 'Settings > Support > About this TV' screen.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic large LG smart TV with unknown exact model/size (worst-case within the shown category).

risks.risk: Screen defects may be missed in normal content (dead pixels/lines often require test patterns).
risks.proof: Video/clip showing full-screen solid colors (red/green/blue/white/black) and a grid/line test, plus close-ups of the panel edges.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if there may be panel issues (worst-case: treat as not guaranteed perfect).

risks.risk: Remote may not be included or may be non-functional.
risks.proof: Photo of the actual remote(s) and a short clip showing basic button response (power/volume/menu).

risks.risk: TV may have been repaired or have panel/backlight issues not visible in photos.
risks.proof: Proof of purchase/warranty card or service receipt; also a power-on self-test/diagnostic screen if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as previously repaired/unknown history (worst-case: not trusted).

risks.risk: Stand/soundbar/other accessories shown may not be included (or may be different from what buyer expects).
risks.proof: A full contents photo listing what is included (TV, stand, remote, power cable, wall mount, soundbar if any).
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming only the TV (and power cable) are included; exclude uncertain accessories.

proof_requests: Clear rear label photo showing exact model number (LG 86UA85006LA or confirm actual model).
A 'Settings > Support > About this TV' screenshot showing model and screen size.
Video test: full-screen color test (red/green/blue/white/black) and grid/line test to confirm no dead pixels/lines.
Photo of the remote and a short clip proving it controls the TV.
Any warranty/service proof or receipt stating 'never repaired' (or at least repair history).
Photo listing all included items (stand type, power cable, remote, any soundbar/extra accessories).
response.reason: LG and webOS are visible, but the critical pricing drivers (exact 86-inch size and the specific model LG 86UA85006LA) are not readable in the photos, and the remote/no-defect/never-repaired claims need test proof. Without those, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
